findings.summary: Lattice-style NTT / ring arithmetic is present: butterflies over a small modulus are the structure post-quantum lattice schemes are built from. This does NOT identify a scheme -- the same ring arithmetic appears wherever that ring is used. And the modulus found is in no published-parameter library, so this is the *shape* of a lattice scheme's arithmetic and not any deployed one's parameters: read it as 'the kernel a lattice scheme is built out of', not as 'a post-quantum implementation'.
findings.title: Classical / PQC style: pqc-style

method.description: Drives the recognized datapath on a fixed, seeded sample of operand vectors because the operand space is too large to enumerate.
method.name: sampled operand evaluation

findings.summary: The same operand registers feed one chain that was verified to compute a + b and one that was verified to compute a - b, at stage depth 1. No constant-operand chain carries it, but the conditional correction on the butterfly subtracts 257 -- derived from the reduction logic and checked on every sum the adder can produce. It is in no library entry. This is lattice-style ring arithmetic; it does not identify a scheme.
findings.title: 1 NTT-style butterfly pair(s) with modulus 257, in no published-parameter library

method.description: Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.

notes: Structure-bounded claims only: every finding is about what the netlist is wired to compute, never about what the design is for.
none-detected is a result, not a failure: it means none of the six passes fired, and the per-pass findings say what each one looked for.
